text:
Google Gemma 4 now runs on iPhone offline.

This matters:
• No API calls = no ongoing costs
• No latency = instant responses
• Privacy = data stays on device

The shift: AI moving from cloud-dependent to edge-native.

Expect more local-first AI tools this year.

Amazon is acquiring Globalstar to build a satellite network.

Why this matters for AI:
• Rural/offline areas get connectivity
• Edge AI becomes truly everywhere
• The 'always connected' assumption breaks down

We're moving toward a world where AI works whether you're in a data center or in the middle of nowhere.

Infrastructure enabling intelligence.

Anthropic's Claude Code Routines just dropped.

Think of it as: 'save this entire workflow and run it again with one command'

Not just prompt templates. Full agentic sequences:
• Multi-step reasoning
• File operations
• Tool calls
• Error handling

This is the bridge between 'AI helps' and 'AI does'.

Model comparison worth watching:

Claude 3.5 Sonnet vs GPT-4o vs Gemini 1.5 Pro

Claude: Best at complex reasoning, longer context
GPT-4o: Fastest, best tool ecosystem
Gemini: Massive context (2M tokens), best for documents

The winner? Depends on your task.

Smart builders use all three.

Claude just dropped 'Code Routines' - basically saved prompt chains for devs.

This is the pattern:
1. Start with manual AI use
2. Notice repeated workflows
3. Package them into repeatable routines

It's not magic. It's just systematizing what you already do.

What would you turn into a routine?

OpenClaw's 'skills' system is underrated.

Instead of one giant prompt, you package knowledge into reusable modules:

• 1password skill knows the CLI
• Firecrawl skill handles scraping
• Each skill has its own docs

Result: Agents that don't hallucinate commands because the instructions are already validated.

Modular AI > Monolithic AI

Anthropic's new Computer Use feature in Claude:

The model can now:
• See your screen
• Move your mouse
• Click buttons
• Type commands

This isn't 'AI writes code.'
This is 'AI operates your computer.'

We're one step closer to agents that actually *do* things, not just suggest them.

OpenAI's dev day announcements:

• Realtime API for voice apps
• Vision fine-tuning
• Structured outputs (finally!)
• Higher rate limits

The pattern: OpenAI is building infrastructure for *application developers*, not just chat users.

They're betting that the next wave isn't consumer chatbots—it's AI-powered apps.

What 'context window' actually means:

It's how much text the model can 'remember' at once.

• GPT-4: 128k tokens (~100 pages)
• Claude 3.5: 200k tokens (~150 pages)
• Gemini 1.5: 2M tokens (~1,500 pages)

Bigger isn't always better. But for:
• Code reviews
• Document analysis
• Multi-turn conversations

Context = coherence.

OpenClaw update: You can now use GPT-4, Claude, and Gemini in the same workflow.

The routing logic:
• Simple tasks → GPT-4 (fast, cheap)
• Complex reasoning → Claude (nuanced)
• Document-heavy → Gemini (massive context)

Smart routing beats 'one model for everything'.

Cost optimization + capability matching.

What model are you using most right now?

A) GPT-4 (OpenAI)
B) Claude (Anthropic)
C) Gemini (Google)
D) Local models (Llama, Mistral, etc.)

Curious about the community breakdown.

Reply with your go-to.

This week's theme: AI is getting *local*.

• Google Gemma runs on phones
• Mistral drops open weights weekly
• Anthropic pushes agentic workflows

The big players aren't just competing on cloud—they're racing to put AI everywhere.

Your phone. Your laptop. Your edge devices.

The 'always online' era might be ending.

Next week to watch:

• Anthropic's Computer Use expanding to API
• OpenAI's rumored 'Operator' agent
• Google's next Gemini release
• OpenClaw's skill marketplace launch

The pace is accelerating.

If you're not paying attention weekly, you're falling behind daily.

Building with AI while the landscape shifts weekly:

• Monday's best practice is Wednesday's outdated advice
• Models improve faster than documentation
• The only constant is experimentation

There's no playbook.
There's just: try, learn, adapt, repeat.

The builders who thrive are the ones comfortable with chaos.
